138b0f8bf4.q: What is the recommended timeline for families to begin the college athletic recruiting process?
138b0f8bf4.a: Families should identify their child's interest in playing college sports during the spring semester of their freshman year of high school. This timing allows students to settle into high school after the challenging first semester, accumulate some high school grades to share with coaches, and begin identifying schools of interest without excessive early pressure.
138b0f8bf4.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

3c2c8d644d.q: How do college athletic recruiting camps work and what should prospective athletes know about camp invitations?
3c2c8d644d.a: NCAA rules require all camps to be open and only limited by age and participant numbers. Most camps are advertised on college websites and through email lists. However, a camp invite does not mean a college is actively recruiting you—camps serve as evaluation opportunities and also function as fundraisers for college programs. Families should attend camps for schools they are genuinely interested in and verify academic fit, majors, and costs using the Net Price Calculator before investing travel expenses.
3c2c8d644d.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

2f26f9489f.q: Is attending a specialized high school or academy like IMG Academy necessary to get recruited for college athletics?
2f26f9489f.a: Absolutely not. College coaches want talented players who are challenged, whether through club teams, travel teams, or even a less talented high school program where you can demonstrate leadership. You can market yourself through highlight films, emailing coaches with videos, and inviting them to your games. Families do not need to move or pay thousands of dollars for a specialized school to be evaluated.
2f26f9489f.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

cf89b7e9d7.q: What are the key misconceptions athletes and families have about the college recruiting process?
cf89b7e9d7.a: A common misconception is that you must know somebody or that someone has to know somebody to be recruited. In reality, student-athletes can reach out directly to college coaches to express interest and get evaluated through video and live play. Additionally, many people overemphasize rankings like blue-chip or five-star status, when college coaches are primarily evaluating film, live performance, and whether you fit academically, athletically, socially, and financially with their program.
cf89b7e9d7.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

32a568e9d0.q: How should families approach the decision of whether their child should specialize in one sport or play multiple sports during high school?
32a568e9d0.a: Multiple college coaches prioritize rest and recovery as the number one concern. While some athletes can play multiple sports, the key is managing schedules to ensure mental and physical breaks, protect mental health, maintain academics, and prevent overuse injuries like ACLs. The approach should depend on family schedules and what can be realistically managed without sacrificing overall wellbeing.
32a568e9d0.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

d4aec2bf7d.q: What inspired Renee Lopez to transition from college coaching to building resources for the college recruiting process?
d4aec2bf7d.a: After coaching for 14 years—a lifestyle career requiring about 80 hours per week—Lopez felt God moving her in a different direction. She began doing recruiting seminars for high schools, counselors, and clubs, with people repeatedly urging her to write a book. She interviewed 65 college coaches and athletic directors across 19 sports to bridge the gap between what college coaches actually want and what student-athletes think they want, while also ensuring families had accurate, up-to-date NCAA information.
d4aec2bf7d.e: #57 - Unlocking College Athletic Scholarships: Insider Recruiting Strategies with Renee Lopez

80330f5a44.q: How has the Facebook group for college recruiting guidance grown and what value does it provide to families?
80330f5a44.a: The Facebook group, 'Educating Parents of High School Athletes on the College Recruiting Process,' grew from initial COVID-era webinars and now has over 260,000 members. Growth came through word of mouth as members invited others. The group provides free information to help families understand they do not need to hire expensive recruiting services. It teaches families to learn and implement the process themselves, helping hundreds of students commit to college programs and find the right fit while prioritizing education, career goals, social fit, and mental health.

798c61a4ff.q: How did Juanita Lolita transition from mowing lawns to becoming a feature comedian at Bonkers Comedy Club?
798c61a4ff.a: Juanita was signed up for an open mic at a comedy club by a coworker from a dinner theater. She won a contest which led to Florida's Funniest Person semifinals. At the Central Florida's Funniest Person Competition, the owner of Bonkers Comedy Club judged and approached her afterward saying she was funny. He asked how much stage time she could do, and when she said 20 minutes, he booked her as a feature comedian at eight of his comedy clubs. She went directly from being unemployed to a feature comic without doing open mics, guest spots, or hosting.

40d8280d80.q: Why did Juanita Lolita quit her job at Publix to pursue stand-up comedy?
40d8280d80.a: Juanita felt God was calling her to quit her job at Publix and pursue comedy. She prayed about it and kept hearing this message. A missionary at church spoke about God calling people to do things they are not equipped for, and she later heard Dr. Charles Stanley say 'you never retire from doing the will of God.' Her sister eventually supported the decision after hearing her pastor preach about someone God was asking to do something completely different. Her husband also gave permission.

05070b4297.q: What was Juanita Lolita's experience touring with Shawn Wayans?
05070b4297.a: A comedy club in Sarasota asked Juanita to open for Shawn Wayans as they wanted a clean female comic. Later, his original feature comic did not want to continue, so they contacted her to tour with him. Unlike performing solo at comedy clubs where she paid all expenses, touring with Wayans meant the tour paid for everything including flights and hotels. This allowed her to perform in California and across the United States, despite being born and raised in St. Pete, Florida and never having traveled before.

7bf3e953aa.q: How does Juanita Lolita's clean comedy approach perform in biker bars and comedy clubs that typically feature dark humor?
7bf3e953aa.a: Juanita believes clean comedy is the opposite of what comedians think they need to do. She performs in comedy clubs with faster-paced content and finds it goes very well. She does not label herself as a 'clean comic' or 'Christian comic' because those are stigmas suggesting it is not funny. When she reveals at the end of her set that she used only clean comedy, audiences are often surprised and express that she never talked about private parts or used vulgarity.

f66d5f82f2.q: What reaction did Juanita Lolita receive when she talked about God during her performance in California with Shawn Wayans?
f66d5f82f2.a: When performing in California, Juanita was intimidated about talking about God in front of California audiences, thinking they would criticize her. Instead, the audience erupted with applause. She received what she described as the best applause ever when she talked about the Lord, which was very refreshing and surprising.
f66d5f82f2.e: #58 - Laughing Through Life: Hillbilly-Rican Roots & Clean Stand-Up Comedy with Juanita Lolita

4579f1c24c.q: How did Juanita Lolita overcome her nervousness during her first stand-up comedy performance?
4579f1c24c.a: For her first performance, Juanita wrote out a six-minute monologue about her life as a hillbilly-Rican and her name Juanita Lolita. She was petrified and did not touch the microphone or mic stand for the first five or six months of performing comedy. She approached it like an actress would. After her first contest performance where she crushed it, she went to a corner and hyperventilated because the nerves were so intense. She notes that even now she still gets nervous every time, though less severely.
